issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path; it gives little guidance on failure cases such as LM output parse errors, rate-limit or API failures, an empty retriever corpus, or a metric that crashes during optimization.

scenarios.name: typed-signature-with-cot
scenarios.rationale: Both define a Signature with a Literal category and a float urgency, wrap it in ChainOfThought, mention `reasoning`, and use dspy.configure(lm=dspy.LM(...)). B's Annotated float with ge/le constrains urgency to 0–1 in the type and its example prints the reasoning, while A only requests the range in the field description and adds optimizer material the task didn't ask for.

scenarios.name: optimize-and-persist-rag-module
scenarios.rationale: Both cover Examples with with_inputs, a train/dev split, a metric with the (example, pred, trace=None) signature, dspy.Evaluate with num_threads, MIPROv2 auto="light", compile on the trainset, .save to JSON, and .load on a fresh module; B adds BootstrapFewShot, cost tracking, a SemanticF1 metric with a custom fallback, and the save_program option, while A is tighter, with a simpler single-file flow and a clear save-only-if-improved gate.

scenarios.name: port-assert-to-refine-3x
scenarios.rationale: Both cover the removal of Assert/Suggest, Refine with N/reward_fn/threshold, BestOfN, the (inputs_dict, prediction) reward_fn signature and dspy.configure(lm=dspy.LM("openai/...")); B explicitly calls the model string LiteLLM-style and keeps the example inside a module, while A adds extra notes (fail_count, Suggest mapping) and says activate_assertions no longer exists, but never uses the LiteLLM label.
